review.tagline: Lets an LLM drive your real Chrome session over a single CDP websocket
review.summary: Browser Harness connects a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex to your own logged-in browser through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. The agent writes missing helper functions into a local workspace file as it works, while the core package under src/browser_harness stays protected. It also ships an MCP server, browser-harness-mcp, that exposes the browser helpers as tools over stdio.
review.audience: Developers giving Claude Code, Codex or MCP clients control of their own browser
strengths: Uses your real browser, so existing logins and sessions are available to the agent
Agent adds its own helpers to agent_helpers.py when one is missing
MCP server over stdio works with Claude Code, Cursor, Devin and other clients
MIT license; install and connection steps documented in install.md
weaknesses: Requires enabling remote debugging in Chrome, which exposes your personal browser to the agent
Parallel browsers, proxies, stealth and CAPTCHA solving are offered only via Browser Use Cloud
Agent-written helpers are not reviewed, so behavior can vary between runs
README gives no model list, hardware needs or test coverage details
needs: Needs Chrome with remote debugging enabled, uv, Python 3.12
Models: Claude Code, Codex, MCP clients
